features.text: The patient is a 58-year-old female.
The patient has been experiencing headaches on the top of her head that come and go.
The headaches are throbbing in nature.
The headaches are sometimes accompanied by dizziness and blurry vision.
The headaches are not usually accompanied by nausea.
The patient has a history of high blood pressure.
The patient is not taking her prescribed medication (chlorthalidone) regularly due to stomachaches.
The patient has been experiencing chest pain sometimes, but not always when she has the headaches.
The chest pain is described as pressure-like, not sharp or dull.
The chest pain lasts for a few minutes and does not have specific triggers.
The headaches have been occurring for about a month.
The headaches are worse when the patient's blood pressure is elevated.
The patient has a history of diabetes.
The patient experiences dizziness and blurry vision during the headaches.
The patient has not had her blood pressure checked recently, but it has been high for a while.
The patient's most recent blood pressure reading was approximately 172/98 mmHg.
The patient does not experience shortness of breath or palpitations.
The patient does not experience changes in vision such as seeing spots or losing vision in one eye during the headaches.
The patient does not have a known family history of hypertension, stroke, or neurological conditions.
The patient does not have a known family history of hypertension, diabetes, or cardiovascular disease.
The patient does not experience weakness, numbness, speech difficulties, or changes in balance beyond occasional dizziness.
